issues: Judged explicitly. Key is correct and the quote is verbatim on the exam guide (Response types: 'Unanswered questions are scored as incorrect; there is no penalty for guessing.'). It satisfies the rule that exam-content claims be sourced to the exam guide. It is appropriate for a Foundation about exam technique (town-charter is a start building whose skill is test-taking), with two cautions: (1) it is the only item in the building that tests exam policy rather than reading scenario keywords, so the building's stated skill ('most cost-effective', 'least operational overhead') is covered by 002-010 and this one is an extra; (2) the stem tells the answer's source ('The exam guide states how unanswered questions are scored'), which is harmless but makes it a recall item. Keep it as difficulty 1; do not tag it for mock-reserve, and do not reuse the claim in a way that depends on the 65/50/15 split (that is exam-guide sourced but not tested here).

Key correct; the target tracking quote ('without manual intervention' on the same page) supports 'least manual intervention'. Key is correct and documented: the s3-storage-classes table row reads 'S3 Standard-IA ... Long-lived, infrequently accessed data (once a month) with millisecond access' and 'S3 Standard ... Frequently accessed data (more than once a month)'. The two quotes used do not contain the 'once a month' wording that the stem depends on, so the access-frequency link rests on inference unless the table row is quoted. S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval and Intelligent-Tiering are not offered, so there is no second defensible answer among the four options.

issues: Stem says 'Only the company's own IAM principals may read them' but the correct option reads 'Grant the application read access through an IAM role' - 'the application' is never introduced in the stem.

S3 Block Public Access limits public access; on its own it does not restrict to the company's principals, so the pairing is defensible only because of the second option. Fine, but the stem should make the requirement ('prevent public access and grant only the application') explicit.
All three wrong options are blatant strawmen (ACL granting all users, Principal * policy, shared access keys); guide says distractors must not be absurd.
suggestedFix: Add 'An application on Amazon EC2 reads the reports.' to the stem and make two distractors subtler (for example 'Grant the application a role with s3:* on all resources' and 'Share a presigned URL with no expiry through email').

issues: Stem puts the 'Application Load Balancer ... in one Availability Zone'. An Application Load Balancer must be configured with subnets in at least two Availability Zones (elastic load balancing docs: 'You must select at least two Availability Zone subnets'), so the premise is technically inconsistent; only the instances can be in one AZ.
Key is otherwise supported by asg-benefits and asg-what-is quotes.
suggestedFix: Reword to 'runs ... on Amazon EC2 instances, all in one Availability Zone, behind an Application Load Balancer.'

issues: Stem constraint contradicts the key: it requires 'keeps the current processing code', but the key has the service poll an SQS queue and the site send to it, which both need code changes.

Evidence is only the generic SQS definition; sqs-what-is also says 'Amazon SQS can process each buffered request independently, scaling transparently to handle any load increases or spikes', a better quote for spikes.
Stem wording 'A review of the existing architecture must find the improvement with the LEAST data loss' is awkward.
suggestedFix: Drop 'that keeps the current processing code' and end with 'Which change prevents orders from being lost during traffic spikes?'. Add evidence 'sqs-what-is|Amazon SQS can process each buffered request independently, scaling transparently to handle any load increases or spikes without any provisioning instructions.'
